questions.q: What are luminous objects? Give examples.
questions.a: Objects that give out their own light - the sun, a candle, a glowing bulb.

questions.q: What are non-luminous objects?
questions.a: Objects that do not make light but are seen by reflected light - moon, chair, book.

questions.q: Why does the moon shine at night?
questions.a: It reflects sunlight - the moon is non-luminous.

questions.q: Define transparent, translucent and opaque objects with examples.
questions.a: Transparent lets light pass clearly (glass); translucent partly (butter paper); opaque not at all (wood).

questions.q: Through which objects can we not see at all?
questions.a: Opaque objects - they block light completely.

questions.q: Which kind of object gives a sharp shadow?
questions.a: An opaque object - it blocks light fully, giving a dark shadow.

questions.q: What three things are needed to form a shadow?
questions.a: A source of light, an opaque object, and a screen (surface) behind the object.

questions.q: Why does a transparent object not cast a shadow?
questions.a: It lets light pass through, so no dark patch forms.

questions.q: Can a shadow form without light? Why?
questions.a: No - a shadow is the blocked light region; without light the idea fails.

questions.q: What decides the length of a shadow?
questions.a: The angle of the light source - low sun gives long shadows, overhead sun short ones.

questions.q: What decides the size of a shadow?
questions.a: The object's size and its distance from the light and screen.

questions.q: Does a shadow show the colour of the object?
questions.a: No - shadows are dark grey/black; colour needs light, which is blocked.

questions.q: How does a pinhole camera form an image?
questions.a: Light from each point passes through the tiny hole in straight lines, making an inverted image on the screen.

questions.q: Why is the pinhole camera's image inverted?
questions.a: Rays cross at the pinhole - top of the object forms the bottom of the image.

questions.q: What happens to the image if the hole is bigger?
questions.a: The image becomes brighter but blurred - overlapping rays spoil sharpness.

questions.q: What does rectilinear propagation of light mean?
questions.a: Light travels in straight lines - shown by sharp shadows and pinhole images.

questions.q: Give two observations proving light moves in straight lines.
questions.a: Sharp shadows of objects and the inverted image of a pinhole camera.

questions.q: Why can we not see around a corner wall?
questions.a: Light travels straight; reflected light from behind the corner cannot reach our eyes.

questions.q: What is reflection of light?
questions.a: Light bouncing back from a surface after striking it - mirrors reflect best.

questions.q: State the law of reflection simply.
questions.a: The angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection.

questions.q: How do we see non-luminous objects?
questions.a: Their surfaces reflect light falling on them into our eyes.
